clue.text: Fatty fish

definitions.meaning: a fat person, in informal slang
a herring cured by smoking whole, ungutted, so it swells

explanation.surface: A plain description of an oily fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a smoked swollen herring and, informally, a fat person, so each clue word is one sense.

clue.text: Mark Antony's extreme spirit

parts.note: a brand is a mark burned or stamped on

indicators.note: extreme means the end letter of the name Antony

explanation.surface: Mark Antony shows extreme spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark Antony' looks like one name, but Mark is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit distilled from wine, a type of strong liquor.

clue.text: Bulbs shining, these charged

parts.note: a lamp that is shining is on
ions are electrically charged particles

explanation.surface: Light bulbs that are shining have been charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulbs' suggests light bulbs; it means vegetable bulbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable grows as an edible bulb, so bulbs is a fair example-type definition.

clue.text: Journey ends in the hajj, entering mass event

parts.note: a journey is a trip

indicators.note: entering means those end letters go inside the word for mass

parts.note: a mass is a lump

indicators.note: ends in means the final letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: The pilgrimage journey ends with a mass gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'the hajj' are E and J, which 'entering' puts inside LUMP. The hajj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca.
explanation.definitionFit: The hop, step and jump is a field event in athletics.

clue.text: Fleet seeks power in attack

indicators.note: in means the letter for power sits inside the word for attack

parts.note: a raid is an attack
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A naval fleet seeks power in an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a noun of ships; it is the adjective meaning swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift, fast-moving.

clue.text: "Fail" about right, poor grade for examination

indicators.note: about means the word for fail goes around the word for right

parts.note: to fail is to lose
OK means all right, correct
E is a low, failing grade on an exam

explanation.surface: A teacher marks a failed test with a poor grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'examination' here means a quick look, not a test, despite the school setting of 'Fail' and 'grade'.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick look or inspection, an informal synonym for a brief examination.

clue.text: Pass up around hip, unwilling to go lower for wrap-around garment

indicators.note: to go lower in a down clue means this piece is placed below the rest
around means the reversed pass encloses the word for hip
up in a down clue means the word for pass is read backwards

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
hip means fashionable, in
loth is a spelling of loath, unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone hitching a garment up around the hip is reluctant to lower it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses and 'to go lower' places a piece underneath; 'around' makes LOINC from the reversed pass and hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth wrapped around the hips is a simple garment, so the description fits.

clue.text: Black and white beast turning up in zebra crossing

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A black and white animal turns up on a zebra crossing, itself black and white.
explanation.walkthrough: ACRO sits inside 'zebra crossing'; 'turning up' reads it upwards in this down clue. A zebra crossing is a British pedestrian crossing painted in black and white stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a marine mammal with striking black and white markings.

clue.text: Stone — rock perhaps describing one

indicators.note: describing means drawing around, so the shuffled letters encircle the numeral
rock means the letters of perhaps are shaken up and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A stone might be a rock describing one thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' turns PERHAPS into SAPPHRE, and 'describing' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue precious gemstone, a kind of corundum.

clue.text: A couple faced listening to what a cow says she does?

indicators.note: listening to means we take the sound of the phrase rather than its spelling

parts.words: what a cow says she does
parts.note: a cow grazing would say I browse

explanation.surface: A couple face each other, listening to a cow describe herself.
explanation.walkthrough: A grazing cow says 'I browse', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: There are two of them on every face, so they are a couple that is faced.

clue.text: Defence shown by boxer with giant cut

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer

indicators.note: cut means the word for giant loses its final letter

parts.note: giant means big

explanation.surface: A boxer's defence against a giant opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims BIG to BI.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of having been elsewhere is a standard defence in a criminal case.

clue.text: See 26
Character billed as land devastated — do nothing about it

indicators.note: about it means the words do and nothing go around the rearranged letters

parts.note: taken as written
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket

indicators.note: devastated means the letters of land are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain is described in a notice as devastating land and doing nothing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'billed' is the joke: the character has a bill, being a bird. A duck is a cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney cartoon duck is a character with a beak, so he is literally billed.

clue.text: Spike Milligan's back scrubbed? God!

indicators.note: scrubbed means a letter is cancelled from the word for spike

parts.note: a spike or prickle is a thorn

indicators.note: back means the final letter of the comedian's name

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that the comedian Spike Milligan's back has been scrubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milligan's back' is N, the last letter, taken from THORN by 'scrubbed'. Spike Milligan was a British comedian of the Goon Show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse god of thunder, wielder of the hammer.

clue.text: Queue up with overseas trader for prayer

definitions.note: read as pray-er, one who prays

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for queue is read backwards

parts.note: a queue is a row of people
someone who ships goods abroad is a shipper

explanation.surface: People queue with a foreign merchant to pray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prayer' must be read as pray-er, a person who prays.
explanation.definitionFit: A congregant at a service is someone who prays, so devotee and petitioner fit.

clue.text: Expectation of rush hour delays, an empty promise?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a traffic hold-up forecast for the next day
the Alice phrase for a treat always promised for later but never delivered

explanation.surface: Commuters are told congestion is coming, a promise that means nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: From Through the Looking-Glass, where the rule is jam yesterday and the next day but never today: a pledge never kept.

clue.text: Arsenic, for example, in it: old meal poisoned

indicators.note: poisoned means the letters of these words are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: Arsenic was in an old meal, which poisoned someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poisoned' rearranges IT, OLD and MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is an element with properties between metals and non-metals, the category named.

clue.text: Perfectionist, model ultimately wearing label

indicators.note: wearing means the label is put on around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a sticker is a label

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word model

explanation.surface: A fussy model ends up wearing a designer label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model ultimately' is L, which 'wearing' puts inside STICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists on exact standards is a fussy perfectionist.

clue.text: Transcontinental location, a Butlins resort

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, means the letters are sorted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A Butlins holiday resort in a far-flung place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as re-sort, rearranging A BUTLINS. Butlins is a chain of British holiday camps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish city straddles the Bosphorus, lying in both Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Demonstrate that it's possible to light up games

definitions.text: Demonstrate that it's possible to light up
definitions.meaning: read literally, try out the little sticks that strike a flame
international cricket fixtures lasting up to five days

explanation.surface: Someone is told to show that lighting up is possible.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the full international fixtures of cricket and rugby, so they are sporting games.

clue.text: Minor left among offspring, having bottom wiped

indicators.note: among means the letter for left goes in with the others
bottom wiped in a down clue means the last letter of the word for offspring is removed

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals

explanation.surface: A small child left among siblings needs a nappy change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having bottom wiped' cuts LITTER to LITTE, and 'among' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor in the sense of small or slight, a direct synonym.

clue.text: At sea, tar yeh?

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of tar and yeh are mixed up

explanation.surface: A pirate addresses a sailor at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges TAR YEH, and the whole clue sketches the pirate's call to a shipmate.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate-speak 'me hearty' addresses a fellow sailor, so a tar at sea fits.

clue.text: Bird jaw

definitions.meaning: a small songbird such as the stonechat
to jaw is to talk idly

explanation.definitionFit: Both are true senses: a small songbird, and talk or gossip, which jaw also means informally.

clue.text: In ecstasy after short film packages endure? That's the stuff of Wallace and Gromit

definitions.text: That's the stuff of Wallace and Gromit

indicators.note: after means these pieces come later in the answer
packages means the word for film wraps around the word for endure

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
to endure is to last
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A film-maker is in ecstasy after a short film packages something durable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packages' makes PLASTIC. Wallace and Gromit are British clay-animation characters.
explanation.definitionFit: The modelling clay used to make the stop-motion Wallace and Gromit films is their material.

clue.text: Fibre found in legumes is a lot

indicators.note: found in means the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Fibre is found in legumes in large amounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant fibre from agave leaves, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Bits of stone balls

definitions.meaning: small particles of stone or sand

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: tiny stone particles, and courage, which balls means in slang.

clue.text: Tough promises by Miliband's lot, or …

parts.note: Ed Miliband led the Labour Party, abbreviated LAB
taken as written
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Labour's promises are tough, the clue running on into the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 26 for the surface only. Ed Miliband led Britain's Labour Party from 2010 to 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Demanding much hard effort, as a tough task is.

clue.text: … safe leader, say, rising to a height of incompetence, as a rule

definitions.text: rising to a height of incompetence, as a rule

parts.note: old underworld slang for a safe, the box a cracksman blows

indicators.note: say means the word for leader is heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a leader or head of a school is a principal

explanation.surface: A safe leader rises until incompetent, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis from 25 is for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The rule observed by Laurence J. Peter that employees are promoted until they reach their level of incompetence.

clue.text: Similar, it's told

explanation.definitionFit: The word means connected or akin, and also recounted, the past participle of relate.

clue.text: Dutch painter admits not all of art good, in general

indicators.note: admits means the painter's name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely, Dutch-born portrait painter

indicators.note: not all of means the word art loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A Dutch painter admits not all his art is good, generally speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all of' and 'admits' make L-ARG-ELY; Lely painted at the court of Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: Mostly, for the most part, which is what in general means.
